title: Files and I/O
summary: Reading and writing text files with java.nio.file - Path and Files, readString, readAllLines, lines and write, BufferedReader and BufferedWriter for large files, character encodings, directories and walking them, handling IOException, parsing CSV records, and the older java.io classes you will still meet.

cards.q: Why read a large file with `Files.lines` or a `BufferedReader` instead of `readAllLines`?
cards.a:
They read one line at a time instead of loading the whole file into memory

`readAllLines` returns a `List` holding every line at once, which can use a lot of memory for a big file. Close `Files.lines` and readers with try-with-resources.

Writing is buffered; closing flushes the remaining data to the file and releases it

Text goes into a buffer first and only reaches the file when the buffer is flushed. Without `close` (or try-with-resources), the last part can be lost.

cards.q: Which builds the path to `data/2026/report.csv` portably?
cards.a:
`Path.of("data", "2026", "report.csv")`

`Path.of` joins the parts with the right separator for the system; gluing strings hard-codes one separator.
